title: Use the Aveva “API page” to interpret Overall System state and select the documented system functions (System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge)
summary: Use the Aveva “API page” (Overall System) to read the current “System State” and interpret what the documented left-side functions do: System Startup, System Bag Out (close out), System Shutdown, and System Purge—specifically including the documented differences between close out vs purge (tote coverage and label printing behavior).
when_to_use: When you need to confirm what the OptiSweep system is currently doing by reading the “System State” on the Aveva “API page,” and you need to explain the documented purpose/behavior of the left-side functions (System Startup, System Bag Out/close out, System Shutdown, System Purge) to guide support actions or troubleshooting discussions.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Access the Aveva “API page,” read the “System State,” and use the documented behaviors of the left-side functions to interpret what the system functions are intended to do.
access_or_tools_needed: Aveva HMI access to the “API page” (Overall System Aveva API page)
Visual access to the left-side sections/labels: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge

access_required: Aveva HMI access to the “API page” (Overall System Aveva API page)

visual_references.description: Overall System Aveva API page frame showing left-side items: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge (including purge vs close out and label printing behavior).

steps.title: Open the Aveva “API page” and locate the left-side items (System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge)
steps.purpose: Establish the correct screen and the specific left-side sections needed to read the current system state and interpret the documented functions.
steps.instruction: On the Aveva HMI, open the Overall System “API page” (referred to as the “API page”). On the left side of the page, locate the labeled sections/items: “System State,” “System Startup,” “System Bag Out,” “System Shutdown,” and “System Purge.”
steps.expected_result: The left side of the Overall System Aveva “API page” shows the labeled items: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, and System Purge.
steps.healthy_condition: All five left-side labels are visible on the Overall System “API page.”
steps.failure_condition: One or more of the expected left-side items (System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge) are not visible on the page you opened.

actions.label: Locate left-side labels on the Overall System API page
actions.exact_action: Locate the left side of your system showing: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the API page does not show the expected left-side items (System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge), stop and escalate for guidance on the correct screen or access.

steps.title: Read the “System State” value to determine the current state the system is in
steps.purpose: Capture the current operational state shown by the system on the Overall System “API page.”
steps.instruction: On the Overall System Aveva “API page,” read the value displayed in the “System State” field.
steps.expected_result: You can point to the current “System State” value shown on the Aveva “API page.”
steps.healthy_condition: A “System State” value is displayed on the page.
steps.failure_condition: The “System State” value is missing/unreadable or the page does not display the System State field.

actions.label: Read System State
actions.exact_action: Read the “System State” value shown on the API page.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the API page does not show the expected left-side items (including “System State”), stop and escalate for guidance on the correct screen or access.

steps.title: Interpret the documented behavior of “System Startup” (AGV staging for exchanges)
steps.purpose: Provide the documented meaning of System Startup so support can interpret what the function is intended to trigger.
steps.instruction: If you need to explain what “System Startup” is intended to do, use the documented behavior shown in the source: AGVs are kept in a shut down state between sorts to allow them to charge, and System Startup triggers OptiSweep to stage the AGVs for exchanges.
steps.expected_result: You can accurately describe that System Startup is associated with staging AGVs for exchanges after AGVs have been kept in a shutdown state between sorts for charging.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation matches the documented behavior: shutdown-between-sorts for charging, then System Startup triggers OptiSweep staging for exchanges.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot explain System Startup using the documented behavior, or you attempt to describe behavior not supported by the source.

actions.label: Use documented System Startup behavior for interpretation
actions.exact_action: System Startup triggers OptiSweep to stage the AGVs for exchanges (AGVs are kept in a shut down state between sorts to allow them to charge).

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not assume behavior beyond what the source states; escalate if the live system behavior contradicts the documented descriptions.

steps.title: Interpret the documented behavior of “System Bag Out” / close out (tote coverage and label printing)
steps.purpose: Provide the documented meaning of System Bag Out/close out so support can interpret what it is intended to do at the end of a sort.
steps.instruction: If you need to explain “System Bag Out” / close out behavior, use the documented behavior: at the end of a sort, close out is used to close all chutes and exchange all totes with items; close out only affects totes with items in it and prints labels.
steps.expected_result: You can accurately describe that close out (System Bag Out) closes all chutes and exchanges totes with items, and that it prints labels for those totes with items.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation matches the documented behavior: close out affects totes with items and prints labels.
steps.failure_condition: You describe close out as exchanging totes without items or as not printing labels, which would contradict the documented behavior.

actions.label: Use documented Bag Out/close out behavior for interpretation
actions.exact_action: At the end of a sort, close out closes all chutes and exchanges all totes with items; close out only affects totes with items and prints labels.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not assume behavior beyond what the source states (e.g., tote coverage and label printing). Escalate if the live system behavior contradicts the documented descriptions.

steps.title: Interpret the documented behavior of “System Shutdown” (AGV charger rotation state)
steps.purpose: Provide the documented meaning of System Shutdown so support can interpret what the system should do when a sort is done.
steps.instruction: If you need to explain “System Shutdown,” use the documented behavior: when the sort is done the system should be put in a shutdown state for AGVs to rotate on the charger.
steps.expected_result: You can accurately describe that System Shutdown is the post-sort shutdown state intended for AGVs to rotate on the charger.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation matches the documented behavior: shutdown state for AGV charger rotation after the sort is done.
steps.failure_condition: You describe System Shutdown as something other than the post-sort shutdown state for AGV charger rotation.

actions.label: Use documented System Shutdown behavior for interpretation
actions.exact_action: When the sort is done the system should be put in a shutdown state for AGVs to rotate on the charger.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not assume behavior beyond what the source states. Escalate if the live system behavior contradicts the documented descriptions.

steps.title: Interpret the documented behavior of “System Purge” (purge everything; no label printing at the tipper)
steps.purpose: Provide the documented meaning of System Purge so support can distinguish purge from close out, including tote coverage and label printing behavior.
steps.instruction: If you need to explain “System Purge,” use the documented behavior: purge is like close out, but instead of only totes with items in it, it will purge everything; it exchanges every tote in the system and does not print a label at the tipper.
steps.expected_result: You can accurately describe that purge exchanges every tote in the system and does not print a label at the tipper (unlike close out which only affects totes with items and prints labels).
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation matches the documented differences: purge covers all totes and does not print a label at the tipper.
steps.failure_condition: You describe purge as only affecting totes with items or as printing labels at the tipper, which would contradict the documented behavior.

actions.label: Use documented System Purge behavior for interpretation
actions.exact_action: Purge exchanges all totes and does not print a label at the tipper (purge everything vs close out only totes with items).

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not assume behavior beyond what the source states (e.g., purge vs close out label printing and tote coverage). Escalate if the live system behavior contradicts the documented descriptions.

success_criteria: You can identify the current “System State” value shown on the Overall System Aveva “API page.”

You can accurately explain the documented purpose/behavior of System Startup, System Bag Out/close out, System Shutdown, and System Purge, including purge vs close out differences (tote coverage and label printing at the tipper).
healthy_conditions: Overall System Aveva “API page” shows the left-side items: System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge.
System State value is visible and readable on the page.
failure_conditions: The Overall System Aveva “API page” does not show one or more expected left-side items (System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge).
Live system behavior contradicts the documented descriptions for purge vs close out (tote coverage and label printing behavior).
escalation_guidance: If the API page does not show the expected left-side items (System State, System Startup, System Bag Out, System Shutdown, System Purge), stop and escalate for guidance on the correct screen or access.
If the live system behavior contradicts the documented descriptions (especially purge vs close out differences), escalate rather than assuming behavior.
